attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, written as a concession inside his argument, not as a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: Fair restatement of a retrospective observation that GPT got more fluent and had many specific mistakes fixed between 2019 and early 2023. The 'compared with GPT-2' qualifier comes from the text. The surrounding claim that core flaws remain is not part of this proposition.

contract.note: The speaker named no measure. The plain reading is fair and ordinary: more natural writing and fewer errors, not zero errors. Treating GPT-3 as a successor within the period is reasonable, though the post's target also covers ChatGPT.

evidence.note: 2021 human-evaluation study. Untrained judges could not tell GPT-3 text from human text better than chance, and the study compares this with GPT-2. That is indirect but relevant evidence of more natural writing.
2021 error-annotation study. Encyclopedic, commonsense and incoherence errors fall from GPT-2 to GPT-3. Some other categories level off, which fits 'lots of', not 'all'.

reviews.rationale: Two independent studies from within the period compare GPT-2 and GPT-3 directly. They show text that reads more like human writing and lower rates in several error categories. Plateaus in other categories do not contradict a claim of 'lots of' fixes, not all. The only gap is that ChatGPT was not tested directly.
